title: Murmuration request scrap notes — probe-ready
content:
Purpose and context:
Quick, messy roll-up of small-scale customer requests and recurring micro-friction notes. Goal: generate 3 low-effort probes (<=3 engineer-days each) we can run this sprint that will (a) validate signal, (b) unblock a few high-friction flows, and (c) feed product/eng decision on a larger feature. This is intentionally rough — treat as a scratchpad.

Topline themes (high frequency across accounts):
- Confusion about "fallbacks" when a dedicated model is saturated — customers expect the shape of response to be identical, but variant fallbacks (quantized vs full-precision) change behavior.
- Prefix/KV cache misses after short-lived autoscale events — some customers see sudden latency spikes for a few minutes after burst traffic.
- Per-route cost visibility is noisy for multi-tenant API keys; customers want quick attribution without cross-team billing noise.
- Desire for a simple UI toggle: "prefer-quality" vs "prefer-latency" per route, not just per model.

Representative raw snippets (verbatim-ish):
- "We had a blip where LLM suggestions went from spot-on to hallucinating for 20m after a capacity failover — our customers trash the feature when it does that." — Customer A
- "Why is my daily cost jump tied to embeddings? We call a rerank that shouldn't be that expensive." — Customer B
- "I toggle dedicated to avoid cold starts but then my app shows different completions vs hosted API — why would it differ?" — Customer C

Clustered feature requests (rough buckets):
1) Fallback fidelity controls
  - Ask: control the "behavioral fidelity" of fallbacks (e.g., strict-kb, permissive).
  - Why: prevents UX regressions when routing to cheaper/quantized variants.
  - Quick probe: add a per-route response-compare flag in the console that logs a small sample of fallback pairs (primary vs fallback) for 24 hours and surfaces mismatch rate.

2) Autoscale cold/ramp cache rehydrate indicators
  - Ask: telemetry + small policy to suppress aggressive batching for first N requests after a scale event, or warm KV-cache proactively.
  - Why: customers report latency spikes lasting ~5–30 minutes after a burst that triggers new GPU nodes.
  - Quick probe: instrument warm-start marker in logs + dashboard card that shows latency percentile only for requests within 10m of scale events. Run for customers X/Y for 2 weeks.

3) Per-route budget attribution (billing clarity)
  - Ask: route-level breakdown that separates generation vs embeddings vs rerank.
  - Why: reduces support back-and-forth and perceived "mystery" bills.
  - Quick probe: expose a new column in Console usage table: "dominant-cost-op" (gen/embed/rerank) computed from sampled calls. Enable for 10 accounts.

4) Prefer-quality vs prefer-latency toggle
  - Ask: UI knob that maps to internal routing policy (prefer lower-latency hardware/variant vs prefer higher-quality model/FP precision).
  - Why: non-engineering PMs want a simple lever.
  - Quick probe: run A/B on new toggle for internal staging accounts and gather feedback from 3 beta customers.

Small engineering notes (rough estimates):
- Fallback sampling probe: ~2 dev-days (1 backend to capture pairs + 1 small console card and SLO alert).
- Scale-event latency card: ~2.5 dev-days (infra telemetry + dashboard query).
- Cost-op sampling column: ~3 dev-days (usage pipeline sampling, small console UI).
- Toggle prototype: ~3 dev-days (routing flag + console toggle + eventing).

Risk & trade-offs (quick list):
- Sampling adds a small extra token cost and storage. Keep samples tiny (<=1% of traffic for large accounts, or capped by count).
- Any feature that surfaces behavioral differences risks surfacing internal complexity to customers; emphasize "actionable" signals and guidance.
- Quick probes should be lightweight and reversible. Do not change default routing behavior in probes (only shadow/log).

Open questions to resolve before an engineering PR:
- How do we define a meaningful "mismatch" between primary and fallback? BLEU/ROUGE is noisy — consider structural checks (length, presence of specific fields, function-call outputs).
- For billing attribution sampling: sample rate that balances accuracy vs cost. Customer B needs near-100% accuracy to reconcile invoicing disputes.
- Which customers to pick for probes? Prioritize customers with frequent incidents OR those that volunteered in support threads.

Immediate next steps (owner + timeline):
- Marisol: assemble 3-customer beta list (due 2027-07-10).
- Ethan: spike telemetry query and prototype a 24-hour fallback mismatch sampler in staging (due 2027-07-12).
- Priya: draft a short note to product/eng prioritization channel summarizing estimated dev-days and ROI (due 2027-07-11).
- Liam: coordinate billing-sample access with finance for two customers (CS-1423) to validate attribution approach (due 2027-07-14).

Metrics to report during probe (minimum):
- Mismatch rate (fallback vs primary) — count and percent per route.
- Latency P95 for requests within 10m of scale events vs baseline.
- % of daily cost attributed to each operation (gen/embed/rerank) by route for sampled accounts.
- Customer qualitative signal: CS score from the beta account + 3 example user quotes.

Quick wins (low friction):
- Console help-text clarification for "fallbacks" and what to expect — one paragraph + link to known-issues. (owner: Product writer, 0.5d)
- Add a single-line log tag on fallback events so CS can query recent fallbacks per api-key (owner: SRE/Eng, 1d)

Notes-to-self (unpolished):
- keep probe sampling off by default. Explicit opt-in from account admin.
- think about long-term: if mismatch detection proves stable, bake into Rollouts page as a fidelity metric for canary decisions.
- flag: add doc snippet for sales/solutions-engineering to set expectations in SOWs around "behavioral variance" when using cheaper model variants.

Decision anchors for final proposal (if probes validate):
- If mismatch rate > 2% for critical routes, propose prioritized roadmap item: "fallback fidelity policies" with a config surface (strict/relaxed/observe-only).
- If scale-event P95 delta > 150ms for >30% of customers in sample, prioritize KV-cache rehydrate work with autoscaler integration.

Links and tickets referenced (quick):
- CS-1423 (billing attribution follow-up)
- FRZ-908 (product doc stub: fallback-expectations)
- PR #498 (routing-sampling spike)

End of note. Keep this doc as living scratchpaper — update after we have initial telemetry (Ethan) and the beta customer list (Marisol).
